lessons.title: The English Alphabet & Short vs. Long Vowel Sounds
lessons.summary: Recognize all 26 letters and contrast short and long vowel pronunciation patterns.
lessons.content: English uses 26 letters (5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U and 21 consonants) to represent 44 distinct sounds. Mastering vowel length distinguishes everyday pairs such as "ship" /ʃɪp/ versus "sheep" /ʃiːp/ and "bit" /bɪt/ versus "bite" /baɪt/.
lessons.pdfContent:
LinguaLearn Study Guide — English Alphabet & Vowel Chart
A /eɪ/ · E /iː/ · I /aɪ/ · O /oʊ/ · U /juː/
Minimal pairs practice: bit/bite, cap/cape, hop/hope, met/meet.

examples.phrase: A — Apple / Cake
examples.translation: Short A vs. Long A diphthong

examples.phrase: E — Pen / Tree
examples.translation: Short E vs. Long E sound

examples.phrase: TH — Think / This

lessons.title: Word Stress, Intonation & Clear Consonant Articulation
lessons.summary: Place primary stress accurately on multi-syllable words and shape natural question intonation.
lessons.content: In English, stressed syllables are louder, slightly higher in pitch, and longer in duration, while unstressed syllables often relax into the schwa /ə/ sound (as in "a-BOUT" /əˈbaʊt/). Rising intonation signals yes/no questions, whereas falling intonation closes wh-questions and statements.
lessons.pdfContent: Two-syllable nouns usually stress the first syllable (PRE-sent, RE-cord), while verbs stress the second syllable (pre-SENT, re-CORD).

examples.phrase: Could you repeat that, please?
examples.translation: Polite rising intonation at the end

examples.phrase: Photographer vs. Photograph

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple in Context
lessons.summary: Choose accurately between completed past time markers and present-connected experiences.
lessons.content: Use Past Simple for actions anchored to a finished time expression ("yesterday", "in 2023", "two hours ago"). Use Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) for life experiences, unfinished time periods ("this week", "so far"), and recent actions with visible results today.
lessons.pdfContent:
Past Simple: Subject + V2 (I visited London in 2024).
Present Perfect: Subject + have/has + V3 (I have visited London three times).

examples.phrase: She has worked here since 2022.
She joined the studio in 2022.

lessons.title: Academic & Workplace Collocations
lessons.summary: Replace vague verbs with natural verb-noun collocations for clear communication.
lessons.content: Fluency depends on knowing which words naturally pair together. Speakers "make a decision" rather than "do a decision", "conduct research" rather than "make research", and "meet a deadline" rather than "reach a deadline".
lessons.pdfContent: High-frequency pairs: conduct research, reach an agreement, draw a conclusion, raise a concern, allocate resources.

examples.phrase: We need to meet Friday’s deadline.
examples.translation: Complete work by the agreed time

examples.phrase: The committee drew a clear conclusion.

lessons.title: Active Listening: Campus Seminar & Briefing Dialogue
lessons.summary: Identify main ideas, speaker attitude, and scheduling details from spoken English.
lessons.content: Listen to the studio announcement carefully: "Good morning everyone. Before we begin Thursday’s design review, please note that the seminar has moved from Room 204 to the North Auditorium at 10:30 AM. Submit your annotated slides by Wednesday at noon so Dr. Vance can prepare feedback."
lessons.pdfContent: Key strategy: Listen for time anchors (Wednesday noon, Thursday 10:30 AM) and location shifts (Room 204 -> North Auditorium).

examples.phrase: The seminar moved from Room 204 to the North Auditorium.

lessons.title: Confident Self-Introductions & Clarifying Questions
lessons.summary: Practice natural pace and polite turn-taking in introductory conversations.
lessons.content: Speak at a steady conversational tempo and link final consonants smoothly to following vowels ("name is" sounds like /neɪ.mɪz/). Practice introducing your role, city, and learning goal.
lessons.pdfContent: Prompt: "Hello, my name is Amina. I study architecture and I am improving my English presentation skills."

examples.phrase: Nice to meet you. Where are you based?

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Urban Bilingualism & Memory
lessons.summary: Analyze evidence, author tone, and inferential claims in an academic passage.
lessons.content: Passage: Longitudinal cognitive studies indicate that adults who regularly alternate between two grammatical systems strengthen executive attention—the mental mechanism responsible for filtering distractions and switching tasks efficiently. While early childhood immersion eases accent acquisition, disciplined adult learners frequently surpass younger learners in syntactic precision and vocabulary retention because they leverage explicit analytical frameworks.
lessons.pdfContent: Focus questions: What advantage do adult learners possess? What does "executive attention" control according to the passage?

examples.phrase: Executive attention filters competing linguistic cues.

lessons.title: Argumentative Essay Structure & Cohesion
lessons.summary: Compose balanced thesis statements, topic sentences, and concession paragraphs.
lessons.content: High-scoring academic essays open with a focused thesis, advance one central claim per body paragraph, and address counterarguments using measured concessions ("Admittedly...", "Nevertheless..."). Avoid unsupported generalizations and use concrete evidence.
lessons.pdfContent: Rubric: Task Response (25%), Coherence & Cohesion (25%), Lexical Resource (25%), Grammatical Range (25%).

examples.phrase: Admittedly, immersion accelerates listening fluency; nevertheless, structured grammar feedback prevents fossilized errors.

lessons.title: L’Alphabet Français, les Accents et la Cédille
lessons.summary: Pronounce all 26 French letters accurately and decode accents (é, è, ê, ç, à).
lessons.content: French shares the 26-letter Latin alphabet with English, yet several letters carry distinctive sounds—especially French "U" /y/ (round lips as for "oo" while saying "ee") and "R" /ʁ/ articulated gently at the back of the throat. Diacritical marks guide pronunciation and meaning: "é" (accent aigu /e/), "è/ê" (accent grave/circonflexe /ɛ/), and "ç" (cédille softening C to /s/ before a, o, u).
lessons.pdfContent:
Accents essentiels:
é = café /ka.fe/
è = mère /mɛʁ/
ç = français /fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
œ = cœur /kœʁ/

examples.phrase: Café · Élève · Français
examples.translation: Accent aigu, grave, and cédille in action

examples.phrase: U vs. OU — Tu / Tout
examples.translation: Front rounded vowel vs. back rounded vowel

lessons.title: Voyelles Nasales et Liaisons Essentielles
lessons.summary: Master nasal vowels (an, on, in) and mandatory spoken liaisons.
lessons.content: When a vowel precedes a silent N or M at the end of a syllable, the sound resonates softly through the nose without pronouncing the consonant: "bon" /bɔ̃/, "pain" /pɛ̃/, "blanc" /blɑ̃/. In connected speech, silent final consonants link onto following vowels, as in "les amis" /le.z‿a.mi/.
lessons.pdfContent: Liaisons obligatoires: article + nom (un ami /œ̃.n‿a.mi/), pronom + verbe (nous avons /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃/).

examples.phrase: Nous avons un ami à Paris.
examples.translation: We have a friend in Paris.

examples.phrase: Bon matin · Pain frais

lessons.title: Passé Composé vs. Imparfait dans le Récit
lessons.summary: Separate background description (Imparfait) from completed plot events (Passé Composé).
lessons.content: Use l’Imparfait for ongoing states, habits, weather, and scenery in the past ("Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti"). Use le Passé Composé (avoir/être + participe passé) for specific, bounded events that move the story forward. Remember DR MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs (aller, venir, partir, arriver) take "être" and agree in gender and number.
lessons.pdfContent:
Imparfait = décor, habitude (je lisais).
Passé Composé = action ponctuelle (j’ai lu ce livre hier).

examples.phrase: Il faisait beau quand nous sommes arrivés.
examples.translation: The weather was nice when we arrived.

examples.phrase: Elle est partie tôt ce matin.
examples.translation: Past participle agrees with feminine subject.

lessons.title: Vocabulaire de la Vie Professionnelle et Quotidienne
lessons.summary: Expand precision with essential French expressions for meetings, travel, and study.
lessons.content: Build natural phrasing beyond literal translation. In French, "to take an exam" is "passer un examen" (not prendre), while "to pass an exam" is "réussir à un examen". Similarly, "avoir besoin de" expresses need and "prendre rendez-vous" schedules an appointment.
lessons.pdfContent: Faux amis à éviter: actuellement = currently (not actually), assister à = to attend, attendre = to wait for.

examples.phrase: Je vais passer mon examen vendredi.
examples.translation: I am going to take my exam on Friday.

examples.phrase: Nous avons besoin d’un rendez-vous.

lessons.title: Compréhension Orale : À la Gare de Lyon
lessons.summary: Follow train announcements, platform changes, and polite ticket counter dialogues.
lessons.content: Écoutez l’annonce : « Mesdames et messieurs, le TGV numéro 6214 à destination de Lyon Part-Dieu, initialement prévu voie H, partira exceptionnellement de la voie M à quatorze heures vingt. Les voyageurs de première classe sont invités à se diriger vers l’avant du quai. »
lessons.pdfContent: Points clés : Numéro du train (6214), destination (Lyon Part-Dieu), changement de voie (H -> M), heure (14h20).

examples.phrase: Le train partira de la voie M à 14h20.

lessons.title: Se Présenter et Commander au Café
lessons.summary: Use polite conditional requests ("Je voudrais...") and warm French greetings.
lessons.content: Politeness is foundational in French conversation: always begin with "Bonjour" before making a request, and prefer "Je voudrais" (I would like) over "Je veux" (I want).
lessons.pdfContent: Phrase modèle : « Bonjour, je voudrais un café crème et un croissant, s’il vous plaît. »

examples.phrase: Bonjour, je voudrais un thé vert, s’il vous plaît.

lessons.title: Lecture Critique : L’Architecture Durable à Paris
lessons.summary: Interpret nuanced journalism on urban ecology, renovation, and civic policy.
lessons.content: Texte : Depuis une décennie, les urbanistes parisiens réinventent l’îlot haussmannien en conciliant préservation patrimoniale et sobriété énergétique. Plutôt que de démolir les immeubles anciens, les architectes privilégient l’isolation biosourcée, la végétalisation des cours intérieures et la transformation des toitures en espaces partagés.
lessons.pdfContent: Lexique : patrimoine (heritage), sobriété énergétique (energy sufficiency), biosourcé (bio-based).

examples.phrase: Concilier préservation patrimoniale et sobriété énergétique.
examples.translation: Balancing heritage preservation with energy efficiency

lessons.title: Rédaction : Le Subjonctif et les Connecteurs Logiques
lessons.summary: Structure formal French arguments using "bien que + subjonctif" and precise transitions.
lessons.content: In DALF-level essays, express necessity, doubt, and concession with the subjunctive: "Il est indispensable que nous agissions", "Bien que cette mesure soit coûteuse...". Connect paragraphs cleanly with "En premier lieu", "Toutefois", and "En somme".
lessons.pdfContent: Connecteurs : D’une part / D’autre part, Toutefois, Néanmoins, Par conséquent, En somme.

examples.phrase: Bien qu’il soit tard, nous devons terminer ce dossier.

lessons.title: Listening Briefing: International Research Collaboration
lessons.summary: Track subtle speaker caveats and budget trade-offs in formal briefings.
lessons.content: Listen carefully: "While our preliminary acoustic trials exceeded baseline clarity by eighteen percent, rolling out the bilingual lab across all twelve partner campuses will require phased training rather than an immediate spring launch."
lessons.pdfContent: Key distinction: trials exceeded clarity by 18%, yet rollout requires phased training.

examples.phrase: Phased training prevents operational bottlenecks.

lessons.title: Lecture Courte : Une Journée à Lyon
lessons.summary: Read a beginner French narrative with present-tense verbs and time expressions.
lessons.content: Texte : Chaque matin, Camille prend le tramway à huit heures pour aller à la bibliothèque universitaire. À midi, elle déjeune avec son frère près du parc de la Tête d’Or. L’après-midi, ils révisent ensemble le vocabulaire anglais et préparent leur exposé.
lessons.pdfContent: Vocabulaire : chaque matin (every morning), déjeuner (to have lunch), réviser (to review).

examples.phrase: À midi, elle déjeune près du parc.
examples.translation: At noon, she has lunch near the park.

lessons.title: Video Lesson: Present Simple & Daily Routines
lessons.summary: Describe daily habits accurately with third-person -s endings and frequency adverbs.
lessons.content: Use Present Simple for routines and permanent facts. Add -s or -es after he, she, and it ("She reads every evening", "He teaches French"). Place frequency adverbs like "always" and "usually" before main verbs, but after the verb "to be".
lessons.pdfContent: Pattern: I/You/We/They work · He/She/It works · Questions: Do you study? Does she study?

examples.phrase: She always reviews her notes before class.
He is usually punctual for morning seminars.

lessons.title: Video Workshop: Leading Meetings & Polite Disagreement
lessons.summary: Use diplomatic phrases to agree partially, ask for clarification, and steer group discussions.
lessons.content: Effective workplace speaking balances clarity with courtesy. Instead of saying "You are wrong", soften disagreements with "I see your point; however, have we considered..." or "Could we revisit the budget timeline?"
lessons.pdfContent: Diplomatic transitions: "I see your point, however...", "Building on Maya’s idea...", "To clarify our next step..."

examples.phrase: I see your point; however, let us review Friday’s deadline.
Building on your proposal, we can test a pilot group first.

lessons.title: Video Seminar: Inversion & Emphasis in Academic Rhetoric
lessons.summary: Master negative adverbial inversion ("Not only did...", "Seldom have...") for persuasive essays.
lessons.content: Placing a negative or restrictive adverbial at the start of a formal sentence triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: "Not only did the cohort improve pronunciation, but their essay cohesion also rose sharply." Use inversion sparingly for high-impact thesis emphasis.
lessons.pdfContent: Structures: Not only + aux + subject + verb · Seldom have we observed · Under no circumstances should...

examples.phrase: Not only did she master phonetics, but she also led the debate.
Seldom have bilingual studies shown clearer gains.

lessons.title: Atelier Vidéo : Exprimer Son Opinion et Nuancer
lessons.summary: Present balanced opinions naturally in French using "À mon avis", "Toutefois", and "Il me semble que".
lessons.content: Pour structurer votre pensée à l’oral comme au DELF B1–B2, annoncez d’abord votre point de vue (« À mon avis », « Je trouve que »), donnez un exemple concret (« Par exemple »), puis nuancez avec « Cependant » ou « D’un autre côté ».
lessons.pdfContent: Expressions clés : À mon avis · Il me semble que · En revanche · Par conséquent.

examples.phrase: À mon avis, l’écoute quotidienne est essentielle.
examples.translation: In my opinion, daily listening is essential.

examples.phrase: Cependant, il faut aussi pratiquer la grammaire à l’écrit.
examples.translation: However, written grammar practice is also needed.

lessons.title: Conférence Vidéo : Journalisme Radiophonique & Rythme
lessons.summary: Follow rapid French broadcast phrasing, elisions, and journalistic synthesis.
lessons.content: Écoutez cet extrait radiophonique : « Selon l’enquête publiée ce matin par l’Observatoire urbain, près de soixante pour cent des municipalités françaises intègrent désormais des matériaux locaux dans la rénovation des écoles publiques. »
lessons.pdfContent: Stratégie C1 : Repérer la source (« Selon l’enquête »), les proportions (« près de 60 % ») et l’enjeu principal.

examples.phrase: Près de soixante pour cent des communes adoptent ce plan.
examples.translation: Nearly sixty percent of municipalities adopt this plan.

lessons.title: Séminaire Vidéo : Les Registres Soutenu et Courant
lessons.summary: Shift seamlessly between everyday spoken French and formal academic or diplomatic vocabulary.
lessons.content: Mastering register means matching vocabulary to the audience. Where everyday speech says "avoir besoin de" or "beaucoup de", formal essays prefer "nécessiter" or "de nombreux". Similarly, "malgré cela" elevates "mais".
lessons.pdfContent: Courant -> Soutenu : comprendre -> saisir · commencer -> entamer · faire -> effectuer · dire -> affirmer.

examples.phrase: Nous devons entamer une analyse approfondie.
examples.translation: We must initiate an in-depth analysis.

examples.phrase: Cette réforme nécessite une concertation étroite.

questions.prompt: Which word contains a long vowel /iː/ sound?
questions.explanation: "Sheep" is pronounced /ʃiːp/ with a long /iː/, whereas "ship" and "bit" use the short /ɪ/.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form: "She ___ (study) English every morning."
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subjects (she/he/it) take -ies for verbs ending in consonant + y.

questions.prompt: Match each English word to its everyday category.
questions.correctAnswer: Library=Place to read books|Schedule=Plan of times|Pronounce=Say a word aloud
questions.explanation: Matching definitions reinforce rapid lexical recall.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words into a polite English question.
questions.explanation: Modal questions begin with "Could + subject + base verb".

questions.prompt: Choose the most accurate tense: "Dr. Vance ___ at Oxford for five years before moving to London in 2021."
questions.explanation: The action finished in a closed past period ("before 2021"), so Past Simple "taught" is required.

questions.prompt: Complete the natural collocation: "Our team worked late to ___ the project deadline."
questions.explanation: In professional English, you "meet a deadline" (not reach or do a deadline).

questions.prompt: Match each verb with its standard academic noun partner.
questions.explanation: Precision with verb-noun collocations distinguishes B2+ proficiency.

questions.prompt: Construct a grammatical sentence using Present Perfect.
questions.explanation: "Since + starting year" pairs with Present Perfect ("has worked").

questions.prompt: Which accent softens the letter "c" to sound like /s/ in "français"?
questions.explanation: The cedilla (ç) turns hard /k/ into soft /s/ before the vowels a, o, and u.

questions.prompt: Complete the polite café order: "Bonjour, je ___ un café, s’il vous plaît."
questions.explanation: "Je voudrais" (I would like) is the standard polite conditional form when ordering.

questions.prompt: Match each French greeting or phrase with its English meaning.
questions.correctAnswer: S’il vous plaît=Please|À demain=See you tomorrow|Enchanté=Nice to meet you

questions.prompt: Arrange the French words to say "We have a friend in Paris."
questions.correctAnswer: Nous avons un ami à Paris
questions.explanation: Standard French declarative word order: Subject + Verb + Object + Location.

questions.prompt: Which auxiliary verb is used in Passé Composé for "partir" (to leave)?
questions.explanation: Verbs of motion like "partir", "arriver", and "venir" form Passé Composé with "être".

questions.prompt: Complete with the right French verb for taking a test: "Je vais ___ mon examen demain."
questions.explanation: "Passer un examen" means to sit/take an exam; "réussir" means to pass it.

questions.prompt: Match each French false friend ("faux ami") to its true English meaning.
questions.explanation: Avoiding false friends prevents frequent B1 translation errors.

questions.prompt: Build the sentence: "She left early this morning."
questions.correctAnswer: Elle est partie tôt ce matin
questions.explanation: Notice feminine agreement on the past participle "partie" with auxiliary "être".

submissions.content: L’été dernier, il faisait très chaud à Lyon. Nous sommes arrivés à la gare le matin et avons visité le Vieux Lyon avant de déjeuner près du fleuve.

forumPosts.title: Best phrases for disagreeing politely in project meetings?
forumPosts.content: I want to sound natural without sounding blunt when suggesting an alternative timeline. Which expressions work best in B1–B2 meetings?

replies.content: Starting with "I see your point, though we might also consider..." works really well in design reviews!

forumPosts.title: Quick tip: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple with time markers
forumPosts.content: Whenever a sentence includes a finished time expression like "last Friday" or "in 2024", stick to Past Simple. Save Present Perfect for unfinished periods like "this week" or experiences.

forumPosts.title: Astuce pour distinguer « u » (/y/) et « ou » (/u/) à voix haute
forumPosts.content: Pour prononcer "tu" correctement, placez vos lèvres comme pour dire "ou" mais essayez de dire "i". C’est très utile pour la différence entre "tu" et "tout" !

replies.content: Merci Amina ! Je vais tester ça dans le Speaking Lab aujourd’hui.

forumPosts.title: Passé Composé : quand accorder le participe passé avec être ?
forumPosts.content: Petit rappel pour le club DELF : avec l’auxiliaire être (aller, venir, partir, arriver), le participe passé s’accorde en genre et en nombre avec le sujet — ex. « Elle est partie tôt ».
